solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree starting to creak when cut

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of creak is kept

blocks.note: first letter of creak
as in 'as I left' means when I left
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A tree begins to groan as it is felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the woodsman's action on the tree, but it is a synonym joined on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a tropical evergreen whose kidney-shaped nuts are eaten worldwide.

clue.text: Make no difference and do what former diamond workers do?

definitions.text: do what former diamond workers do?

blocks.note: first meaning: an idiom for having no effect or influence

blocks.clueFragment: do what former diamond workers do?
blocks.note: second meaning, playful: ice is slang for diamonds, and retired diamond cutters no longer cut it

explanation.walkthrough: Ice is old slang for diamonds; workers who are former cutters now cut none, which is the joke behind the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut no ice is an idiom meaning to fail to impress or influence anyone.

clue.text: Jammin' party that's hard to see for all the wood?

definitions.text: that's hard to see for all the wood?

blocks.note: jamming something is sticking it in, read as two words
a sect is a faction or party

explanation.surface: A reggae get-together so crowded in the woods you can't spot it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition twists 'can't see the wood for the trees': this creature looks so like a twig that it vanishes among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stick insects are camouflaged insects shaped like twigs, so they are almost invisible among branches.

clue.text: For this reason stroppy sort rolled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, rolling something up runs it from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: an ogre is a bad-tempered, fearsome person

explanation.surface: Because of this, a bad-tempered person was wrapped up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is the Latin-derived word meaning therefore, used to introduce a conclusion.

clue.text: Cheerful line adopted by rustic

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the first piece is placed inside the second

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
a rustic is a country dweller, a peasant

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin takes up a happy line of talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustic' reads as an adjective but serves as a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant manner is friendly and agreeable, close in sense to cheerful.

clue.text: Pay attention being unusually silent at uni, say

indicators.note: doing something unusually means not in the normal way, so these letters are put in another order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
a British student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: An instruction to concentrate, odd because the student is quiet at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go up to Oxford or Cambridge, and are up while in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: Listen up is an informal command telling people to pay attention to what follows.

clue.text: Speak ill of plan to retain new trailer

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so the first word keeps the letter inside it

blocks.note: an aim is a plan or intention
N is the abbreviation for new
a film trailer is an advertisement for it

explanation.surface: Criticise a scheme for keeping a fresh film preview.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert is a formal verb meaning to criticise or pass censure on something.

clue.text: Article on mimic causes trouble

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
to do someone is to impersonate them

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about an impressionist stirs up bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the second piece after the first in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Male in the grip of blue ideal

indicators.note: being held in someone's grip means being enclosed by them, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
blue is the colour of the British Conservative or Tory party

explanation.surface: A man held captive by a melancholy perfectionist dream.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue means sad on the surface; in British politics it stands for the Conservatives, also called Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Theory is the abstract, idealised version of things, as opposed to practice.

clue.text: Bishop to dip into funds?

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to dip into a book is to read bits of it

explanation.surface: A churchman raiding the collection money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dip into' looks like one phrase meaning to raid savings; it splits, with 'into' joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, from the idea of earning one's daily bread.

clue.text: Famous horse set off TV sweep?

blocks.note: first meaning: Roy Rogers' palomino in American western films
second meaning: to start or cause something, a verb
third meaning: the dim road sweeper in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: 'sweep' here is a road sweeper, not a chimney sweep or a sweepstake.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cowboy's horse, a verb for starting something off, and a sitcom character who sweeps streets.

clue.text: Miss Spain's shout that approves support for one going downhill

blocks.note: to skip something is to miss it out
olé is the Spanish cry of approval

explanation.surface: A beauty queen from Spain cheers on someone in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Spain' looks like a beauty title, but the words split: Miss is a verb and Spain introduces the cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier pushes off and balances on poles while descending a slope.

clue.text: When son goes to the back drench trees

indicators.text: When son goes to the back
indicators.note: the letter for son is moved from the front of the word to its end

blocks.note: to drench is to soak

explanation.surface: When the boy goes out back, he hoses down the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the abbreviation for son; here it is already the first letter of the word and travels to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaks are large broadleaf trees of the genus Quercus, bearing acorns.

clue.text: Criminal chap with relevant detail

blocks.note: a chap is a man, a male
a factor is a circumstance that bears on an outcome

explanation.surface: A crook with information that matters to the case.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a formal word for a wrongdoer or criminal.

clue.text: Re-employing that epicure could be relaxing

indicators.note: employing the letters again in a new way means rearranging them

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Hiring the gourmet again might be soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something therapeutic has a healing, calming effect, so it is relaxing.

clue.text: A little problem cutting grass

indicators.note: something cutting into a word splits it apart and sits between its halves

blocks.note: to grass and to sing are both slang for informing to the police
as in 'what's the matter?'

explanation.surface: A minor mower fault while trimming the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the lawn being cut; it is British slang for informing, which also gives sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a small amount, especially a slight knowledge of something.

clue.text: Pictures blokes going back into shadowy agency

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left
into means placed inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: Photos of men retreating into a secret spy service.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is an old British way of saying going to the cinema.

clue.text: Scope is not quite clean on inspection

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: pure means clean
an inspection is a viewing

explanation.surface: A telescope that looks almost spotless when examined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scope' tempts as an instrument; it means range or remit.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview is the range of someone's authority or concern, their scope.

clue.text: Ratty rant was about opening from mostly sham argument

indicators.note: an opening is the start of something, so the first letter of the word is taken
ratty means irritable and out of sorts, so these letters are disordered
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap around the single letter

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
first letter of mostly

explanation.surface: An irritable outburst full of mostly bogus reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like a deletion signal on 'sham'; it is only the source of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw man is a distorted version of an opponent's case, set up only to be knocked down.

clue.text: Home alone and likely to stay in vogue

blocks.note: first meaning: without a romantic date, so stuck in for the evening
second meaning: timeless, never going out of fashion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Home alone' evokes the film, but it just describes someone with no partner for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lacking a date and timeless, so never dated or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Conceive and slowly develop grand property

blocks.note: G is short for grand, slang for a thousand
an estate is landed property

explanation.surface: Dreaming up and gradually building a splendid house and land.
explanation.definitionFit: To gestate is to carry young in the womb, and figuratively to let an idea mature over time.

clue.text: A drama unfolds as one sails into sight

indicators.note: unfolding opens something out into a different shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene plays out as a ship appears on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read as a fleet coming into view as one, all sails together.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Panels of poets grasping nothing

indicators.note: grasping means holding tight, so the outer word closes around the other

blocks.note: bards are poets
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Committees of poets clutching at nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Boards are flat sheets of wood, and also panels of people such as a board of directors.

clue.text: Explain Government deficiency

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for government
a loss is a shortfall or deficit

explanation.surface: Account for the state's budget shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss a text is to add notes interpreting its difficult words or passages.

clue.text: Potter's play is done here being up for debate

blocks.note: first meaning: a snooker player pots balls, and play happens on the baize
second meaning: offered for discussion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests a ceramicist or Harry Potter, but it is anyone potting balls in snooker or pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal on the table has been put forward for discussion, while snooker is literally played on a table.

clue.text: Plot against English monk and historian

blocks.note: a bed is a garden plot
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A medieval chronicler scheming against his own country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a conspiracy; it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was an eighth-century Northumbrian monk who wrote an early history of the English church.

clue.text: Overload one hire vehicle

blocks.note: to tax is to strain or burden
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Cram a single rented car too full.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a car that can be hired with its driver for individual journeys.

clue.text: Fantastic serial on motorway — it shows it like it is

definitions.text: it shows it like it is

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly unreal, so these letters are rearranged into fantasy

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
M is the British prefix for motorways, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A wonderful drama series set on a motorway that tells the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' is ironic: fantasy is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism in art or writing depicts life accurately, without idealisation.

clue.text: Couple avoiding soft look

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: a pair is a couple
p is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Two people steering clear of a gentle glance.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or appearance, as in an air of confidence.

clue.text: Right time to infiltrate old spook

indicators.note: infiltrating means slipping inside, so the pair goes within the other word

blocks.note: stale means old, no longer fresh
R is the abbreviation for right
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The ideal moment to plant a veteran spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spook' looks like a noun for a spy, but it is the verb meaning to frighten.
explanation.definitionFit: To spook someone is to frighten them suddenly, which is what startle means.

clue.text: Wild gardens, home to cold ingredient for stew?

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
being home to something means housing it, so the letter sits inside

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Overgrown gardens shelter a chilly item for the casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters wrap the single letter after the fourth position.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag end is the bony neck of mutton, a cheap British cut used in stews.

clue.text: For the most part debate pitching event?

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to debate is to discuss

explanation.surface: Mostly a debate about whether to throw the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitching' sounds like a sales pitch for a debate; it is throwing, as in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus is an athletics field event in which a heavy disc is thrown for distance.
